draft.title: Rising seas after the ice age
card: During the last ice age, huge amounts of water were frozen as ice. Sea levels were much lower, so more land was dry than today.
Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea were joined as one large landmass. People could walk between these places.
As the ice age ended, the ice melted and the seas rose. Water flooded low land, cutting off Tasmania and New Guinea and forming the Torres Strait Islands.
Oral traditions of First Nations Australians tell of land lost to the sea. They are stories passed down by speaking over many generations.
draft.remember: Melting ice raised the seas, and First Nations oral traditions tell of the land that was lost.

a.q: Why did Tasmania become an island at the end of the last ice age?
opts: Melting ice raised the seas and flooded low land
Falling seas left Tasmania standing high above the water
A drier climate caused the land to sink into the sea
Rising seas pushed Tasmania away from the mainland
a.why: Ice that had been frozen melted and ran into the oceans, so seas rose and covered low land that once joined Tasmania to the mainland. Falling seas would have done the opposite, joining places rather than cutting them off.
a.clue: Think about what happened to the frozen water when the ice melted.

b.q: Mia hears an Elder tell a story, handed down over many generations, about land that was once dry and is now under the sea. What does the story most likely show?
opts: An oral tradition that tells of land lost to rising seas
A written record made by the first European sailors
A story about animals that lived in Australia long ago
A tale about how people first learned to make stone tools
b.why: The story describes dry land that the sea later covered, which matches the rising seas after the ice age. Passing it on by speaking makes it an oral tradition, not a written record.
b.clue: Look at how the story was passed on and what it describes.

a.best: Melting ice raised the seas and flooded low land

b.best: An oral tradition that tells of land lost to rising seas

problems.detail: The stem already says the story is handed down over generations and is about dry land now under the sea. The right option just restates this, and the other options are about unrelated topics or contradict the stem (a written European record). A student can pick it by matching words without knowing what an oral tradition is.
